newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile police fail to find German colony leader.
newsitem.headline: Chile police fail to find German colony leader.

text.p: Chilean police vowed on Thursday to continue their search after a raid on a secretive German colony failed to flush out fugitive leader Paul Schaefer, who faces charges of sexually molesting boys at the settlement.
"The investigations have not been exhausted. We cannot rule out more raids," said police commander Mario Flores.

Nearly 200 police on motorcycles, horseback and in trucks left after an 11-hour search on Wednesday at the Colonia Dignidad (Dignity Colony), which lies in the woodlands of the Andean foothills 200 miles (322 km) south of Santiago.
Local news media reported that police arrested about a dozen settlers during the raid for resisting attempts to search their houses.
The raid followed a series of brief police inspections that began last month at the colony of traditional Bavarian-style homes.
Interior Minister Carlos Figueroa said police found a secret network of tunnels at the colony which was founded by Schaefer in 1961.
Television images showed police dogs clawing at wood-tile floors which proved to have false bottoms covering entrances to tunnels.

Opponents of the colony said Chileans have lost patience with the attempts by the settlers to protect Schaefer which have included sending an imposter to register as the colony leader at a hotel in the Argentine resort Bariloche during the weekend.
"Chileans' patience is reaching its limit," said the secretary of the Christian Democrat party Rafael Moreno.
"(The colonists) have abused our country and showed sarcasm towards our legislation, our police and our courts."

Schaefer, who has not been seen in public for years, is the subject of an international arrest warrant after being accused last year of sexually assaulting at least five Chilean boys at a boarding school run by the colony.
Colonia Dignidad's leaders have also been charged with child abduction, obstruction of justice and tax evasion.
Several hundred German-speaking settlers live behind barbed wire at the colony and have very little contact with the outside world.
Defectors from the colony say residents are not allowed to read newspapers or watch television, their mail is censored and youngsters are subjected to unusual punishments by Schaefer.
